what: Polymarket Perps maker book shape: calibration parameters for a seeded synthetic flow generator (Task B)

core_hours_utc.role: busy (most trades of 21 full hours; contains the 13:30 UTC US cash open)
quiet (fewest trades of 21 full hours; first hour after the US cash close)

sample.hour_selection_method: full hours only (2026-09-29T14, T17, T18 partial/empty and T15 has a recorder restart; 2026-09-30T15 still recording); ranked by count of trade records in trades:: frames (settlement=false; no settlement trades were seen)
sample.which_sample_for_what: Book shape (spread, gaps, levels, distance, depth, dust, repeats) from the 3 core hours = 950,488 snapshots x up to 40 levels. Requote vs trades per market and the per-hour robustness table from all 21 full hours (the thin markets have few trades per hour).
sample.book_source: book::<iid> frames: 20-level snapshots (both sides), recorder keeps the last frame of each server-time second, so 1 snapshot per market per second (checked: consecutive snapshots are exactly 1000 ms apart in ets). Only the top 20 levels per side are visible.
sample.per_market_counts_core3: each market has ~10,800 snapshots (3 x 3600); pooled statistics weight markets equally in time

units_and_conversions.engine: price in ticks of 10^-pd USD, size in lots of 10^-qd units, pd+qd=6 so ticks x lots = micro-dollars (docs/DECISIONS.md D-004)
units_and_conversions.real_tick_rule: real_tick_engine_ticks = 10^max(0, digits(price_ticks) - 5)  (5 significant figures; equivalent to max(10^-pd, 10^(floor(log10 price) - 4)) USD)
units_and_conversions.real_tick_rule_check: core3: 0 share of 35,043,924 visible levels off this grid; every spread and every level gap is an integer number of real ticks
units_and_conversions.real_tick_bps: real_tick_usd / mid * 1e4; ranges 0.10-2.3 bps across the 88 markets, so a spread or gap in real ticks is NOT comparable across markets without it
units_and_conversions.bps_to_ticks: ticks = max(1, round(bps / real_tick_bps)) then engine ticks = ticks * real_tick_engine_ticks

rule.alt_crypto: category=crypto, not a major, max_leverage >= 10 (exchange tier max_market_notional 500k or 1M)
rule.tradfi: category in {equity, index, commodity}; supplementary split tradfi_macro = SP500, NAS100, GOLD, SILVER, WTIOIL, BRENTOIL and tradfi_equities = the other 42

classes.why: Majors are tick-bound (1-tick spread). The two crypto classes follow the exchange's own leverage tiers and differ in depth and dust. Tradfi books are deeper (fixed $25k/$50k/$100k clips), but about half of their seconds see no requote. In the macro sub-class, SP500, NAS100 and GOLD are tick-bound like the majors, and all six are much deeper than single stocks; use it where a flow needs it.

markets.note: shape columns from core3; *_all21 columns from all 21 full hours

generator_recipe: 1. Give each synthetic market a class and a price; real tick = 10^max(0, digits(price_ticks)-5) engine ticks; tick_bps = real tick / price.

2. Spread: tick-bound markets (majors; SP500, NAS100, GOLD) sample real ticks from by_class.majors.spread.real_ticks.pmf. Other markets: sample spread_bps ~ lognormal(spread.bps.ln_mean, ln_sd) of their class (or use the market row), ticks = max(1, round(bps / tick_bps)).

3. Ladder: 20 levels per side (thin classes: draw the count from levels_per_side). Gap to the next level: sample real ticks from gap_between_levels.by_level_index[1-4 | 5-9 | 10-19].ticks_pmf; the >10 tail: lognormal in bps (bps_ln_mean, bps_ln_sd) converted to ticks.

4. Depth per level: with prob by_level_index[k].dust_share put a $10-12.5 dust order; else draw from model_B: a clip from the clip menu (share-weighted, USD x U(0.95,1.05), lots fixed per market for a while) or the background lognormal. Level 1 is thin (median $1-3k), levels 3-10 carry the clips.
5. Reuse the same clip lots at several levels and on both sides (this is what produces the ~35% exact-size repeats); dust levels repeat their size ~86% of the time.

6. Requotes: per market, level-change events at rate requote.per_market_nonfill_changes_per_s (lognormal across markets), mix ~37% add / 37% remove / 13% size up / 13% size down, ~50% at levels 1-5, bursty per second (see nonfill_changes_in_one_second_pmf_buckets); >=1000 changes per trade overall. These are LOWER BOUNDS on maker messages.
caveats: Only the top 20 levels per side are visible; levels_per_side is min(true count, 20) and depth beyond level 20 is unknown.

Requote counts are 1-second net level diffs: a level changed and restored within a second, or changed twice, counts once or zero; they are lower bounds on maker messages. Changes at a price that traded on that side in the same second are excluded (fill-attributed); 22% of trades print at a price not resting on the maker side in the previous snapshot (the level appeared within the second).
Window-edge effects are removed: only prices inside both snapshots' visible ranges are compared (naive whole-window diffs are 13% higher).
Trade counts per market are small (thin markets have 0-10 trades per hour), so per-market changes-per-trade ratios for thin markets are noisy even over 21 hours.
Class pooled real-tick distributions mix markets with different tick_bps; for non-tick-bound markets use bps and convert per market.
Depth percentiles use log bins of 1/100 decade (2.3% wide), interpolated; the clip-menu windows are +-7% and include some background mass.
US-equity-hours dependence: tradfi requote rate at 13 UTC (US open) is 3.5-5.4x the other two core hours; shape parameters vary much less across hours (per_hour_robustness_all21).
validation: Independent re-count (Decimal arithmetic, separate script book_work/spotcheck.py) for BTC-USD and DOGE-USD in 2026-09-30T10 reproduces the pipeline: naive changes/s 13.72 and 11.52, dust share 0.0001 and 0.132, BTC spread 1 real tick, DOGE spread median 45 real ticks.
core3 sanity counters: 0 crossed/locked books, 132 one-side-empty snapshots (long-tail), 0 snapshot gaps over 1.5 s, 0 off-grid levels, 0 non-integer spreads or gaps in real ticks.
